transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, thank you for seeing me. I um... I guess what brings me in is that I keep getting these just awful, awful doubts that I've missed something important. And it's honestly exhausting. I mean, I'm a graphic designer, I've been doing this for years, and being detail-oriented is obviously part of the job, but this has gone way beyond normal professional diligence. It's this constant, nagging terror that I've overlooked something catastrophic. 

Like, I'll be reviewing a client proof, and I'll suddenly panic that I missed a really important clause or messed up the text. Or I'll be doing my personal finances and I'll become absolutely convinced that I missed a number on the mortgage payment. Or even just simple things, like leaving the house, I'll be certain a door is not latched. 

And the worst part is, I know I checked it. I will literally stand there and check the door or stare at the document on my screen, and I know in my logical brain that it's completely fine. But it just doesn't matter. The thought just barges right back in anyway, almost immediately, and it's always this heavy, looming dread. It just screams at me, what if this is the mistake that costs you everything? What if this is the one tiny oversight that ruins your business or loses the house? And I just can't shake it, I try to tell myself it's fine but it just loops and loops and I don't know how to make it stop.

When these doubts come up, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking things over and over, mentally reviewing events, or trying to neutralize the thoughts in a specific way—to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, exactly, that is exactly what I do. It’s like I can’t just let it be. If I finish up a project, I end up reopening the files... I mean, I’ll close out of my design software, tell myself it’s done, and then two minutes later, that panic hits, and I’m opening it right back up just to make absolutely sure the bleed margins were right or the layers were flattened. And then I close it, and then I do it again. 

And the emails, oh my goodness, I will sit there rereading emails I’ve already sent to clients, just scanning and scanning to make sure I didn't type something completely wrong or forget an attachment. 

And with the financial stuff, like I was saying before, I’ll go in and keep checking the online payment confirmation. I'll log into my bank portal, look at the confirmation screen, log out, and then the doubt hits again, so I log right back in to check it a second time, or a third time, or a fourth time. 

And if I'm not at my desk, like if I can't physically check the screen to reassure myself, I do this... this mental thing. I'll start saying the figures silently in my head. Just repeating the invoice total or the account numbers over and over to myself while I'm driving or making dinner. I just keep saying them until they finally feel... I don't know, "settled," I guess? Like until my brain finally accepts that the numbers are correct and the dread lifts just a tiny bit. 

But it takes so long to get to that settled feeling. And as a freelancer, you know, time is money. I've been in this industry a long time, and I pride myself on efficiency, but lately, this whole process turns a simple invoice or a tiny, minor logo revision into hours of work. Just hours and hours that I absolutely cannot bill for. I mean, I can't exactly charge a client for the three hours I spent reopening their PDF and repeating numbers in my head, so I just eat the cost. And it's just... it's ruining my productivity, it really is, and I just get so mad at myself for wasting all this time when I have so many other things I need to be doing...

Can you tell me if the thoughts or images that come to you when you're doubting yourself are things you actually want or intend, or if they feel more like something you don't want and are trying to resist?

Oh, no, no, no, I definitely don't want them. That's the thing that's so incredibly frustrating about all of this. It's not like I'm sitting there trying to think up worst-case scenarios, you know? It's the exact opposite. I am desperately trying to focus on my work, or on just living my life, and these thoughts just... they intrude. They just barge right in, completely uninvited. 

Like I was saying before, about the doubts that I've missed something important? That's exactly it. It's this awful, awful doubt that I've overlooked a number on the mortgage payment, or missed a crucial clause in a client proof, or even just left a door unlatched. And I don't want to be thinking about that! I want to be thinking about the color palette for the new branding package I'm working on, or what I'm going to make for dinner, or literally anything else. But it just forces its way into my brain.

And the thing is, I try so hard to push it away. I try to resist it. I'll tell myself, "You checked the door, it's fine," or "You proofread that document three times, there are no errors." And for a split second, I might actually believe it. But then, almost immediately, the thought just barges right back in again, louder than before, going, "But what if? What if this is the mistake that costs you everything? What if this is the one tiny oversight that ruins your business or loses the house?" 

It's like my brain is actively working against me. I'm trying to be logical, I'm trying to be rational, because I *know* I checked whatever it is. But the dread just overwhelms the logic. It's like a physical weight, this heavy, looming feeling that something catastrophic is going to happen if I don't pay attention to the thought. So I end up fighting it and fighting it, and it's just so exhausting. I absolutely do not want these thoughts, I just want them to stop so I can have some peace and quiet in my own head for once.

Other candidates (F41.0, F40.1, F43.30) are ruled out due to better fit with OCD diagnostic criteria.
